source: Audited statements for Surat Municipal Corporation — 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24

response.intro: In FY 2023-24, Surat Municipal Corporation reported a total revenue of INR 4,406.82 crore and a total expenditure of INR 7,603.58 crore, implying that its expenditure accounted for 173% of its revenue

data.name: Total Revenue Receipts (Cr)
data.info:
1. What is Total Revenue Receipts?

  • It indicates the revenue receipts a ULG earns or receives from tax and non-tax sources including revenue grants and assigned revenues.

2. How is it calculated?

Total Revenue Receipts is the sum of:

  1. Own Source Revenue
  2. Assigned Revenue
  3. Revenue Grants
  4. Others

data.name: Total Expenditure (Cr)
data.info:
1. What is Total Expenditure?

  • It indicates a ULG's total spending on capital expenditure and revenue expenditure.

2. How is it calculated?

Total Expenditure = Capital Expenditure + Revenue Expenditure

  • Revenue expenditure is the sum of:
    1. Establishment Expenditure
    2. Administrative Expenditure
    3. O&M Expenditure
    4. Interest and Finance Charges
    5. Other line items (program expenses, depreciation, etc.)
  • Capital Expenditure is the sum of:
    1. Net Block (Gross Block + Accumulated Depreciation (negative figures))
    2. Capital Work in Progress

data.name: Total Debt (Cr)
data.info:
1. What is Total Debt?

  • It indicates a ULG's standalone debt obligations.

2. How is it calculated?

Total Debt = Secured Loans + Unsecured Loans

data.name: Total Expenditure to Total Revenue Receipts (%)
data.info:
1. What is Total Expenditure to Total Revenue?

  • It indicates the extent of a ULG's spending against its total receipts.
  • A higher ratio (>100%) indicates the ULG is spending more than it earns. A lower ratio (<100%) reflects a surplus.

2. How is it calculated?

Total Expenditure over Total Receipt

Total Expenditure is the sum of Capital Expenditure and Revenue Expenditure.

  • Capital Expenditure is the sum of the following:
    1. Net Block (Gross Block + Accumulated Depreciation (negative figures))
    2. Capital Work in Progress
  • Revenue expenditure is the sum of the following:
    1. Establishment Expenditure
    2. Administrative Expenditure
    3. O&M Expenditure
    4. Interest and Finance Charges
    5. Other 8 line items

Total Receipts is the sum of Capital Receipts and Revenue Receipts.

  • Capital Receipts is the sum of:
    1. Debt Income (Secured and Unsecured Loans)
    2. Non-Debt Income (Capital Grants and Sale of fixed assets)
  • Revenue Receipts is the sum of:
    1. Own Source Revenue
    2. Assigned Revenue
    3. Revenue Grants
    4. Others

data.name: Own Source Revenue to Total Revenue Receipts (%)
data.info:
1. What is Own Source Revenue to Total Revenue?

  • It indicates the extent to which a ULG's revenue is generated from its own source revenues (such as property tax, rental income from municipal properties, fees and user charges, etc.) against total revenue receipts.
  • A higher ratio (above 50%) is desirable indicating greater self-reliance and reduced dependence on revenue grants and assigned revenues.

2. How is it calculated?

Own Source Revenue over Total Revenue Receipts

Own Source Revenue is the sum of the following:

  1. Tax Revenue
  2. Rental Income
  3. Fee & User Charges
  4. Sale & Hire Charges
  5. Interest Earned
  6. Income from Investment
  7. Other Income

Total Revenue Receipts is the sum of the following:

  1. Own Source Revenue
  2. Assigned Revenue
  3. Revenue Grants
  4. Others

data.name: Grants to Total Revenue Receipts (%)
data.info:
1. What is Grants to Total Revenue?

  • It indicates the extent to which a ULG's revenue is supplemented by revenue grants against total revenue receipts.
  • A lower ratio is desirable indicating greater self-reliance and reduced dependence on revenue grants and assigned revenues.

2. How is it calculated?

Revenue Grants over Total Revenue Receipts

Total Revenue Receipts is the sum of the following:

  1. Own Source Revenue
  2. Assigned Revenue
  3. Revenue Grants
  4. Others

data.name: Own Source Revenue to Total Expenditure (%)
data.info:
1. What is Own Source Revenue to Total Expenditure?

  • It indicates the extent to which a ULG's total expenditure is covered by its own source revenues.
  • A higher ratio is desirable indicating greater self-reliance with a higher share of expenditure being met from the ULG's own source revenue.

2. How is it calculated?

Own Source Revenue over Total Expenditure

Own Source Revenue is the sum of:

  1. Tax Revenue
  2. Rental Income
  3. Fee & User Charges
  4. Sale & Hire Charges
  5. Interest Earned
  6. Income from Investment
  7. Other Income

Total Expenditure is the sum of Capital Expenditure and Revenue Expenditure.

  • Revenue Expenditure is the sum of:
    1. Establishment Expenditure
    2. Administrative Expenditure
    3. O&M Expenditure
    4. Interest and Finance Charges
    5. Other line items (program expenses, depreciation, etc.)
  • Capital Expenditure is the sum of:
    1. Net Block (Gross Block + Accumulated Depreciation (negative figures))
    2. Capital Work in Progress

data.name: Capital Expenditure to Total Expenditure (%)
data.info:
1. What is Capital Expenditure to Total Expenditure?

  • It indicates the extent to which ULG's expenditure is directed toward creating or upgrading long-term assets against the total expenditure.
  • A higher ratio (above 50%) indicates higher focus on infrastructure creation and asset-building. A lower ratio indicates a stronger focus on recurring expenses.

2. How is it calculated?

Capital Expenditure over Total Expenditure

Total Expenditure is the sum of Capital Expenditure and Revenue Expenditure.

  • Revenue expenditure is the sum of:
    1. Establishment Expenditure
    2. Administrative Expenditure
    3. O&M Expenditure
    4. Interest and Finance Charges
    5. Other line items (program expenses, depreciation, etc.)
  • Capital Expenditure is the sum of:
    1. Net Block (Gross Block + Accumulated Depreciation (negative figures))
    2. Capital Work in Progress

data.name: Operating Revenue Surplus (Cr)
data.info:
1. What is the Operating Revenue Surplus?

  • It indicates the available surplus/deficit generated from recurring revenue receipts and expenses.
  • A higher surplus is desirable indicating greater available cashflows to service debt and invest in infrastructure development.

2. How is it calculated?

Operating Revenue Surplus = Revenue Receipts - Revenue Expenditure (without interest and depreciation)
